claim: Fertilization occurs before the completion of oocyte meiosis in the majority of animal species.
source: Fertilization occurs before the completion of oocyte meiosis in the majority of animal species and sperm contents move long distances within the zygotes of mouse and C. elegans.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general biological fact about animal reproduction.

claim: Sperm contents move long distances within the zygotes of mouse and C. elegans.
source: Fertilization occurs before the completion of oocyte meiosis in the majority of animal species and sperm contents move long distances within the zygotes of mouse and C. elegans.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Katanin and kinesin-13 limit long-range movement of sperm contents in C. elegans.
source: Through live imaging of fertilization in C. elegans, we found that the microtubule disassembling enzymes, katanin and kinesin-13 limit long-range movement of sperm contents and that maternal ataxin-2 maintains paternal DNA and paternal mitochondria as a cohesive unit that moves together.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 5.

claim: Maternal ataxin-2 maintains paternal DNA and paternal mitochondria as a cohesive unit that moves together.
source: Through live imaging of fertilization in C. elegans, we found that the microtubule disassembling enzymes, katanin and kinesin-13 limit long-range movement of sperm contents and that maternal ataxin-2 maintains paternal DNA and paternal mitochondria as a cohesive unit that moves together.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: Depletion of katanin resulted in the capture of the sperm contents by the meiotic spindle.
source: Depletion of katanin or double depletion of kinesin-13 and ataxin-2 resulted in the capture of the sperm contents by the meiotic spindle.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 5.

claim: Double depletion of kinesin-13 and ataxin-2 resulted in the capture of the sperm contents by the meiotic spindle.
source: Depletion of katanin or double depletion of kinesin-13 and ataxin-2 resulted in the capture of the sperm contents by the meiotic spindle.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 9.

claim: Limiting movement of sperm contents contributes to preventing premature interaction between maternal and paternal genomes.
source: Thus limiting movement of sperm contents and maintaining cohesion of sperm contents within the zygote both contribute to preventing premature interaction between maternal and paternal genomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: Maintaining cohesion of sperm contents within the zygote contributes to preventing premature interaction between maternal and paternal genomes.
source: Thus limiting movement of sperm contents and maintaining cohesion of sperm contents within the zygote both contribute to preventing premature interaction between maternal and paternal genomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: A Ran-GTP gradient emanating from the mouse metaphase II meiotic spindle excludes the fusion proteins Juno and CD9 from the oocyte plasma membrane over the spindle.
source: A Ran-GTP gradient emanating from the mouse metaphase II meiotic spindle excludes the fusion proteins Juno and CD9 from the oocyte plasma membrane over the spindle.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: When the Ran-GTP exclusion mechanism was bypassed by injecting demembranated sperm adjacent to the spindle, the sperm DNA was ejected into a polar body in mouse oocytes.
source: When this mechanism was bypassed by injecting demembranated sperm adjacent to the spindle, the sperm DNA was ejected into a polar body (Mori et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: In C. elegans, the nucleus is positioned away from the site of future fertilization so that the meiosis I spindle assembles at the opposite end of the ellipsoid zygote from the site of fertilization.
source: In C. elegans, the nucleus is positioned away from the site of future fertilization so that the meiosis I spindle assembles at the opposite end of the ellipsoid zygote from the site of fertilization (Panzica and McNally, 2018; McNally et al., 2010; McCarter et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: Cytoplasmic streaming can move the sperm DNA long distances in both mouse and C. elegans.
source: However, simply controlling the site of fertilization is not sufficient to maintain a distance between the meiotic spindle and the sperm DNA because cytoplasmic streaming can move the sperm DNA long distances in both mouse (Mori et al., 2021) and C. elegans (Panzica et al., 2017; Kimura and Kimura, 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: Meiotic cytoplasmic streaming in C. elegans embryos requires microtubules.
source: Meiotic cytoplasmic streaming in C. elegans embryos requires microtubules (Yang et al., 2003), kinesin-1 (McNally et al., 2010), and reticulons (Kimura et al., 2017), but both mechanism and purpose are not completely understood.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: Meiotic cytoplasmic streaming in C. elegans embryos requires kinesin-1.
source: Meiotic cytoplasmic streaming in C. elegans embryos requires microtubules (Yang et al., 2003), kinesin-1 (McNally et al., 2010), and reticulons (Kimura et al., 2017), but both mechanism and purpose are not completely understood.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: Meiotic cytoplasmic streaming in C. elegans embryos requires reticulons.
source: Meiotic cytoplasmic streaming in C. elegans embryos requires microtubules (Yang et al., 2003), kinesin-1 (McNally et al., 2010), and reticulons (Kimura et al., 2017), but both mechanism and purpose are not completely understood.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: C. elegans meiotic embryos have cytoplasmic microtubules around the cortex and throughout the cytoplasm of the entire embryo.
source: In addition to meiotic spindle microtubules, C. elegans meiotic embryos have cytoplasmic microtubules around the cortex and throughout the cytoplasm of the entire embryo (McNally et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: Depletion of tubulin stops cytoplasmic streaming in C. elegans.
source: These microtubules are thought to drive meiotic cytoplasmic streaming because depletion of tubulin stops cytoplasmic streaming (Yang et al., 2003) and depletion of the microtubule-severing protein katanin by RNAi results in an increased mass of cortical microtubules and an increase in cytoplasmic streaming (Kimura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: Depletion of katanin by RNAi results in an increased mass of cortical microtubules and an increase in cytoplasmic streaming.
source: These microtubules are thought to drive meiotic cytoplasmic streaming because depletion of tubulin stops cytoplasmic streaming (Yang et al., 2003) and depletion of the microtubule-severing protein katanin by RNAi results in an increased mass of cortical microtubules and an increase in cytoplasmic streaming (Kimura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: C. elegans sperm introduce centrioles, SPE-11 protein, membranous organelles (MOs), and paternal mitochondria into the zygote.
source: In addition to paternal DNA, C. elegans sperm introduce centrioles, SPE-11 protein, membranous organelles (MOs), and paternal mitochondria into the zygote.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Paternal centrioles are silenced during meiosis by maternal KCA-1.
source: Paternal centrioles are silenced during meiosis by maternal KCA-1 (McNally et al., 2012), which is also required to pack yolk granules inward from the cortex (McNally et al., 2010) and the meiotic spindle outward toward the cortex (Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: KCA-1 is required to pack yolk granules inward from the cortex.
source: Paternal centrioles are silenced during meiosis by maternal KCA-1 (McNally et al., 2012), which is also required to pack yolk granules inward from the cortex (McNally et al., 2010) and the meiotic spindle outward toward the cortex (Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: KCA-1 is required to position the meiotic spindle outward toward the cortex.
source: Paternal centrioles are silenced during meiosis by maternal KCA-1 (McNally et al., 2012), which is also required to pack yolk granules inward from the cortex (McNally et al., 2010) and the meiotic spindle outward toward the cortex (Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: SPE-11 is an RNA-binding protein in sperm.
source: SPE-11 is an RNA-binding protein in sperm (Li et al., 2023) that is required paternally for polar body extrusion (McNally and McNally, 2005) and proper embryonic development (Hill et al., 1989; Browning and Strome, 1996).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: SPE-11 is required paternally for polar body extrusion.
source: SPE-11 is an RNA-binding protein in sperm (Li et al., 2023) that is required paternally for polar body extrusion (McNally and McNally, 2005) and proper embryonic development (Hill et al., 1989; Browning and Strome, 1996).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: SPE-11 is required for proper embryonic development.
source: SPE-11 is an RNA-binding protein in sperm (Li et al., 2023) that is required paternally for polar body extrusion (McNally and McNally, 2005) and proper embryonic development (Hill et al., 1989; Browning and Strome, 1996).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: MOs are membrane vesicles in sperm that fuse with the sperm plasma membrane before fertilization during sperm activation.
source: MOs are membrane vesicles in sperm that fuse with the sperm plasma membrane before fertilization during sperm activation (L'Hernault, 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: A subset of MOs that do not fuse with the sperm plasma membrane are introduced to the zygote at fertilization and are ubiquitinated with maternal ubiquitin.
source: However, a subset of MOs that do not fuse with the sperm plasma membrane are introduced to the zygote at fertilization and are ubiquitinated with maternal ubiquitin (Molina et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: Paternal mitochondria are labeled with maternal autophagy machinery.
source: Paternal mitochondria are labeled with maternal autophagy machinery (Sato and Sato, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation.

claim: During meiosis, MOs and paternal mitochondria remain in a tight cloud around the sperm DNA.
source: Whereas both MOs and paternal mitochondria are eventually destroyed during embryogenesis, during meiosis they remain in a tight cloud around the sperm DNA (Panzica et al., 2017; Molina et al., 2019; Sato and Sato, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by citations.

claim: ER is distributed throughout the zygote during meiosis.
source: Time-lapse in utero imaging of the meiotic spindle and an endoplasmic reticulum marker (ER) revealed that the ER is distributed throughout the zygote but appears as undulating lines during metaphase I (n=8), changes to a dispersed appearance during anaphase I (n=9), transitions back to undulating lines interspersed with large blobs during metaphase II (n=6), then changes to a dispersed pattern during anaphase II (n=5) (Figure 1A; Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is a finding from live imaging experiments shown in Figure 1A.

claim: ER appears as undulating lines during metaphase I.
source: Time-lapse in utero imaging of the meiotic spindle and an endoplasmic reticulum marker (ER) revealed that the ER is distributed throughout the zygote but appears as undulating lines during metaphase I (n=8), changes to a dispersed appearance during anaphase I (n=9), transitions back to undulating lines interspersed with large blobs during metaphase II (n=6), then changes to a dispersed pattern during anaphase II (n=5) (Figure 1A; Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is a finding from live imaging experiments shown in Figure 1A.

claim: ER changes to a dispersed appearance during anaphase I.
source: Time-lapse in utero imaging of the meiotic spindle and an endoplasmic reticulum marker (ER) revealed that the ER is distributed throughout the zygote but appears as undulating lines during metaphase I (n=8), changes to a dispersed appearance during anaphase I (n=9), transitions back to undulating lines interspersed with large blobs during metaphase II (n=6), then changes to a dispersed pattern during anaphase II (n=5) (Figure 1A; Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is a finding from live imaging experiments shown in Figure 1A.

claim: ER transitions back to undulating lines interspersed with large blobs during metaphase II.
source: Time-lapse in utero imaging of the meiotic spindle and an endoplasmic reticulum marker (ER) revealed that the ER is distributed throughout the zygote but appears as undulating lines during metaphase I (n=8), changes to a dispersed appearance during anaphase I (n=9), transitions back to undulating lines interspersed with large blobs during metaphase II (n=6), then changes to a dispersed pattern during anaphase II (n=5) (Figure 1A; Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is a finding from live imaging experiments shown in Figure 1A.

claim: ER changes to a dispersed pattern during anaphase II.
source: Time-lapse in utero imaging of the meiotic spindle and an endoplasmic reticulum marker (ER) revealed that the ER is distributed throughout the zygote but appears as undulating lines during metaphase I (n=8), changes to a dispersed appearance during anaphase I (n=9), transitions back to undulating lines interspersed with large blobs during metaphase II (n=6), then changes to a dispersed pattern during anaphase II (n=5) (Figure 1A; Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is a finding from live imaging experiments shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The undulating lines of ER correspond to sheet-like ER.
source: Previous electron microscopy studies have indicated that the undulating lines correspond to sheet-like ER and the dispersed appearance corresponds to tubular ER (Poteryaev et al., 2005; Gong et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated based on previous electron microscopy studies cited.

claim: The dispersed appearance of ER corresponds to tubular ER.
source: Previous electron microscopy studies have indicated that the undulating lines correspond to sheet-like ER and the dispersed appearance corresponds to tubular ER (Poteryaev et al., 2005; Gong et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated based on previous electron microscopy studies cited.

claim: A similar transition to sheet-like ER during mitotic M phase has been reported in HeLa cells.
source: A similar transition to sheet-like ER during mitotic M phase has been reported in HeLa cells (Lu et al., 2009) and Xenopus egg extracts (Wang et al., 2013), however, this may not be universal in all cell types (Puhka et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated based on previous studies cited.

claim: A similar transition to sheet-like ER during mitotic M phase has been reported in Xenopus egg extracts.
source: A similar transition to sheet-like ER during mitotic M phase has been reported in HeLa cells (Lu et al., 2009) and Xenopus egg extracts (Wang et al., 2013), however, this may not be universal in all cell types (Puhka et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated based on previous studies cited.

claim: Yolk granules are packed inward, away from the cortex during meiosis.
source: In striking contrast with the ER filling the entire zygote, yolk granules are packed inward, away from the cortex (n=9 metaphase I; Figure 1B) as previously described (McNally et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a finding from fixed embryo imaging shown in Figure 1B and supported by a citation.

claim: Paternal mitochondria are found in a discrete cloud around the paternal DNA.
source: When Mitotracker-treated males were mated to hermaphrodites expressing GFP-labeled yolk granules, the paternal mitochondria were found in a discrete cloud around the paternal DNA (n=34; Figure 1B–C) as previously described (Sato and Sato, 2011).
evidence: This is a finding from fixed embryo imaging shown in Figure 1B-C and supported by a citation.

claim: The cloud of paternal mitochondria is observed in cortical regions that are free of yolk granules.
source: Both the cloud of paternal mitochondria (n=19) and the meiotic spindle (n=9 metaphase I) were observed in cortical regions that are free of yolk granules (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from fixed embryo imaging shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The meiotic spindle is observed in cortical regions that are free of yolk granules.
source: Both the cloud of paternal mitochondria (n=19) and the meiotic spindle (n=9 metaphase I) were observed in cortical regions that are free of yolk granules (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from fixed embryo imaging shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Maternal mitochondria are packed inward, away from the cortex.
source: Maternal mitochondria labeled with COX-4::GFP were also packed inward, away from the cortex, and were excluded from the cloud of paternal mitochondria and excluded from the spindle (n=5 metaphase I; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from fixed embryo imaging shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Maternal mitochondria are excluded from the cloud of paternal mitochondria.
source: Maternal mitochondria labeled with COX-4::GFP were also packed inward, away from the cortex, and were excluded from the cloud of paternal mitochondria and excluded from the spindle (n=5 metaphase I; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from fixed embryo imaging shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Maternal mitochondria are excluded from the spindle.
source: Maternal mitochondria labeled with COX-4::GFP were also packed inward, away from the cortex, and were excluded from the cloud of paternal mitochondria and excluded from the spindle (n=5 metaphase I; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from fixed embryo imaging shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The cloud of paternal mitochondria remains together and separate from maternal yolk granules even when moving long distances with cytoplasmic streaming.
source: Time-lapse imaging (n=21) revealed that the cloud of paternal mitochondria remained together and separate from maternal yolk granules even when moving long distances with cytoplasmic streaming (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In kca-1(RNAi) meiotic embryos, yolk granules do not pack and instead extend to the plasma membrane.
source: In kca-1(RNAi) meiotic embryos, yolk granules (McNally et al., 2010) and mitochondria (Figure 2A and B) do not pack and instead extend to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a finding from RNAi experiments shown in Figure 2 and supported by a citation.

claim: In kca-1(RNAi) meiotic embryos, mitochondria do not pack and instead extend to the plasma membrane.
source: In kca-1(RNAi) meiotic embryos, yolk granules (McNally et al., 2010) and mitochondria (Figure 2A and B) do not pack and instead extend to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a finding from RNAi experiments shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Maternal mitochondria are still excluded from the volume of paternal mitochondria in kca-1(RNAi) embryos.
source: Maternal mitochondria were still excluded from the volume of paternal mitochondria in kca-1(RNAi) embryos (n=11 control, 8 RNAi; Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from RNAi experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The volume of paternal mitochondria excludes maternal mitochondria.
source: This result indicated that the volume of paternal mitochondria excludes maternal mitochondria.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kca-1(RNAi) experiment results.

claim: Paternal mitochondria form a discrete cluster in meiotic embryos of a nematode species with giant sperm.
source: In addition, paternal mitochondria also formed a discrete cluster in meiotic embryos of a nematode species with giant sperm (Vielle et al., 2016) (n=4; Figure 2C) indicating that the unique properties of the ball of paternal organelles in the meiotic zygote are conserved.
evidence: This is a finding from experiments with C. macrosperma shown in Figure 2C and supported by a citation.

claim: The unique properties of the ball of paternal organelles in the meiotic zygote are conserved between nematode species.
source: In addition, paternal mitochondria also formed a discrete cluster in meiotic embryos of a nematode species with giant sperm (Vielle et al., 2016) (n=4; Figure 2C) indicating that the unique properties of the ball of paternal organelles in the meiotic zygote are conserved.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the C. macrosperma experiment results.

claim: Maternal ER penetrates into the cloud of paternal mitochondria and envelops the paternal DNA in a shell.
source: In contrast with maternal yolk granules and maternal mitochondria, maternal ER was observed penetrating into the cloud of paternal mitochondria and enveloping the paternal DNA in a shell that appeared as a ring in confocal sections of both live and fixed meiotic embryos (n=10; Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from live and fixed embryo imaging shown in Figure 3A.

claim: C. elegans sperm fuse with the egg as opposed to being phagocytosed.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that C. elegans sperm fuse with the egg as opposed to being phagocytosed (Takayama and Onami, 2016).
evidence: This is stated based on a previous study cited.

claim: 20 seconds after the apparent entry of paternal mitochondria into the egg, a sperm-sized volume devoid of maternal ER is observed within the maternal plasma membrane.
source: 20 s after the apparent entry of paternal mitochondria into the egg (0:20 in Figure 3B), a sperm-sized volume devoid of maternal ER was observed within the maternal plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 3B.

claim: One minute after apparent sperm-egg fusion, the maternal ER had moved into the plasma membrane behind the sperm.
source: One minute after apparent sperm-egg fusion, the maternal ER had moved into the plasma membrane behind the sperm (1:25 in Figure 3B; 1:00 in Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: The maternal ER ring enveloping the sperm DNA is not discernible until 7 minutes after apparent sperm-egg fusion.
source: The maternal ER ring enveloping the sperm DNA was not discernible until 7 min after apparent sperm-egg fusion (7:24 in Figure 3C), although it might form earlier because the zygote undergoes dramatic movement through two sequential sphincters into the spermatheca then into the uterus during this time.
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The envelopment of the sperm DNA by maternal ER may be an initial step in nuclear envelope assembly.
source: The envelopment of the sperm DNA by maternal ER may be an initial step in nuclear envelope assembly (Penfield et al., 2020; Barger et al., 2023), which has been halted until after the completion of meiosis.
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations.

claim: Maternal ER is initially excluded from the sperm at fusion.
source: These results show that maternal ER is initially excluded from the sperm at fusion.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the time-lapse imaging results.

claim: All maternal membranes are initially excluded from the sperm at fusion.
source: Since maternal mitochondria and yolk granules are excluded later, this suggests that all maternal membranes are initially excluded from the sperm at fusion.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that maternal ER, mitochondria, and yolk granules are all excluded.

claim: The plasma membrane marker diffuses in behind the sperm first, followed by plasma-membrane-associated ER, followed by envelopment of the sperm DNA by maternal ER by 7 minutes after fusion.
source: The plasma membrane marker diffuses in behind the sperm first, followed by plasma-membrane-associated ER, followed by envelopment of the sperm DNA by maternal ER by 7 min after fusion.
evidence: This is a summary of the temporal sequence observed in the time-lapse imaging.

claim: Maternal yolk granules and maternal mitochondria are excluded from the sperm volume for much longer than 7 minutes after fusion.
source: Maternal yolk granules and maternal mitochondria, however, are excluded from the sperm volume for much longer (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the timing of ER entry with the exclusion of yolk granules and mitochondria.

claim: BAF-1 is a chromatin-binding component of the inner nuclear envelope.
source: To test whether the ER envelope around the sperm DNA is permeable to proteins, we analyze BAF-1, a chromatin-binding component of the inner nuclear envelope (Gotzmann and Foisner, 1999).
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: Maternally provided GFP::BAF-1 is not detected on maternal or paternal chromatin during metaphase I or metaphase II.
source: Maternally provided GFP::BAF-1 was not detected on maternal or paternal chromatin during metaphase I or metaphase II but labeled the surface of both maternal and paternal chromatin during anaphase I and anaphase II (Figure 4A, B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from live and fixed embryo imaging shown in Figure 4.

claim: GFP::BAF-1 labels the surface of both maternal and paternal chromatin during anaphase I and anaphase II.
source: Maternally provided GFP::BAF-1 was not detected on maternal or paternal chromatin during metaphase I or metaphase II but labeled the surface of both maternal and paternal chromatin during anaphase I and anaphase II (Figure 4A, B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from live and fixed embryo imaging shown in Figure 4.

claim: BAF-1 can pass freely through holes in the ER envelope surrounding the sperm DNA between metaphase I and anaphase I.
source: Because BAF-1 is a chromatin-binding protein, this result indicates that BAF-1 can pass freely through holes in the ER envelope surrounding the sperm DNA between metaphase I and anaphase I.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the BAF-1 localization results.

claim: A previous study found that the male pronucleus very rarely forms at the same end of the embryo as the female pronucleus.
source: C. elegans meiotic cytoplasmic streaming (McNally et al., 2010; Panzica et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2003; Kimura et al., 2017) has the potential to bring the sperm contents into close proximity with the meiotic spindle, however, a previous study found that the male pronucleus very rarely forms at the same end of the embryo as the female pronucleus (Kimura and Kimura, 2020).
evidence: This is stated based on a previous study cited.

claim: Limitations on cytoplasmic streaming might be involved in maintaining distance between the sperm contents and the meiotic spindle.
source: This indicates that limitations on cytoplasmic streaming might be involved in maintaining distance between the sperm contents and the meiotic spindle.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that male and female pronuclei rarely form together.

claim: Depletion of kinesin-13 by klp-7(RNAi) increases the mass of cortical microtubules.
source: Depletion of katanin by mei-1(RNAi) increases the mass of cortical microtubules and the extent of yolk granule streaming (Kimura et al., 2017) and depletion of kinesin-13 by klp-7(RNAi) also increases the mass of cortical microtubules (Gigant et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: mei-1(RNAi) or klp-7(RNAi) increased the maximum displacement of the sperm contents in both the long and short axes of the ellipsoid embryo relative to control L4440(RNAi) embryos.
source: We found that mei-1(RNAi) or klp-7(RNAi) increased the maximum displacement of the sperm contents in both the long and short axes of the ellipsoid embryo relative to control L4440(RNAi) embryos (Figure 5A, B, C and D; Figure 5—videos 1–3).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 5.

claim: Excessive streaming in klp-7(RNAi) persists for a longer period of time, well into metaphase II.
source: The only demonstrably significant difference between the excessive cytoplasmic streaming in these two depletions was that excessive streaming in klp-7(RNAi) persists for a longer period of time, well into metaphase II (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Among 15 control L4440(RNAi) time-lapse sequences, the closest center-to-center distance between spindle and sperm contents was 18 µm.
source: Among 15 control L4440(RNAi) time-lapse sequences, the closest center-to-center distance between spindle and sperm contents was 18 µm.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: Among 51 time-lapse sequences of mei-1(RNAi) meiotic embryos, the sperm came within 5.5 µm center to center distance of the spindle in 12 cases.
source: In contrast, among 51 time-lapse sequences of mei-1(RNAi) meiotic embryos, the sperm came within 5.5 µm center to center distance of the spindle in 12 cases, and in 12/12 of these cases, the sperm stopped moving relative to the spindle indicating a capture event (Figure 5B; Figure 5—video 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from time-lapse imaging experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In 12/12 cases where the sperm came within 5.5 µm of the spindle in mei-1(RNAi) embryos, the sperm stopped moving relative to the spindle indicating a capture event.
source: In contrast, among 51 time-lapse sequences of mei-1(RNAi) meiotic embryos, the sperm came within 5.5 µm center to center distance of the spindle in 12 cases, and in 12/12 of these cases, the sperm stopped moving relative to the spindle indicating a capture event (Figure 5B; Figure 5—video 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from time-lapse imaging experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Among a subset of mei-1(RNAi) embryos that could be tracked through the pronuclear stage, a single male pronucleus formed adjacent to multiple small female pronuclei.
source: Among a subset that could be tracked through the pronuclear stage, a single male pronucleus formed adjacent to multiple small female pronuclei.
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: Among 25 time-lapse sequences of klp-7(RNAi) embryos, the sperm DNA became stuck against the meiotic spindle (4.6 µm center to center distance) in only one case.
source: Among 25 time-lapse sequences of klp-7(RNAi) embryos, the sperm DNA became stuck against the meiotic spindle (4.6 µm center to center distance) in only one case.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: In all other klp-7(RNAi) cases, the sperm streamed past a stationary spindle.
source: In all other cases, the sperm streamed past a stationary spindle.
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: Limiting cytoplasmic streaming is important for maintaining a distance between spindle and sperm and thus preventing the capture of the sperm by the meiotic spindle.
source: These results indicate that limiting cytoplasmic streaming is important for maintaining a distance between spindle and sperm and thus preventing the capture of the sperm by the meiotic spindle.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mei-1(RNAi) and klp-7(RNAi) experiments.

claim: mei-1(RNAi) spindles are apolar and do not undergo normal polar body extrusion.
source: However, mei-1(RNAi) spindles are apolar and do not undergo normal polar body extrusion, and the single capture event in a klp-7(RNAi) embryo resulted in cell cycle arrest.
evidence: This is stated as a known property of mei-1(RNAi) spindles.

claim: The single capture event in a klp-7(RNAi) embryo resulted in cell cycle arrest.
source: However, mei-1(RNAi) spindles are apolar and do not undergo normal polar body extrusion, and the single capture event in a klp-7(RNAi) embryo resulted in cell cycle arrest.
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: During metaphase I, when the ER is sheet-like, the movement of the sperm contents is limited.
source: During metaphase I, when the ER is sheet-like, the movement of the sperm contents is limited.
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: When the ER disperses during anaphase I, the spindle rotates and one pole is moved closer to the cortex by cytoplasmic dynein.
source: When the ER disperses during anaphase I, the spindle rotates and one pole is moved closer to the cortex by cytoplasmic dynein (Figure 1—video 1; Ellefson and McNally, 2011).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging and supported by a citation.

claim: The distance of the sperm contents from the cortex increases when the ER disperses.
source: In contrast, the distance of the sperm contents from the cortex (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) and the movement of the sperm contents both increase when the ER disperses (Figure 5C; Figure 5—video 4).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The movement of the sperm contents increases when the ER disperses.
source: In contrast, the distance of the sperm contents from the cortex (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) and the movement of the sperm contents both increase when the ER disperses (Figure 5C; Figure 5—video 4).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The C. elegans ortholog of ataxin-2, ATX-2, affects ER organization.
source: Because maternal ER penetrates the sperm contents and envelops the sperm DNA, and because the C. elegans ortholog of ataxin-2, ATX-2, affects ER organization (Del Castillo et al., 2019), we analyzed the contribution of ATX-2 to the cohesion of the sperm contents in meiotic embryos.
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: Endogenously tagged ATX-2 is observed throughout oocytes and meiotic embryos.
source: Endogenously tagged ATX-2 was observed throughout oocytes and meiotic embryos (Figure 6B and C; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from live imaging of endogenously tagged ATX-2 shown in Figure 6.

claim: ATX-2 does not uniquely co-localize with ER.
source: ATX-2 did not uniquely co-localize with ER (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from imaging shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dark holes were observed in ATX-2 localization suggesting exclusion from the lumens of larger membranous organelles.
source: Dark holes were observed suggesting exclusion from the lumens of larger membranous organelles (Figure 6C; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from imaging shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: 1-hr auxin, 24 hr GFP(RNAi), or 27 hr atx-2(RNAi) all resulted in a significant reduction of the ATX-2::AID::GFP signal.
source: We then compared the intensity of the GFP signal after three different depletion treatments, 1- hr auxin, 24 hr GFP(RNAi), or 27 hr atx-2(RNAi). All three methods resulted in a significant reduction of the GFP signal (Figure 6B, C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence intensity measurements shown in Figure 6D.

claim: ATX-2 depletion by each of the three methods resulted in a significantly increased mean distance of paternal mitochondria from the sperm DNA.
source: ATX-2 depletion by each of the three methods resulted in a significantly increased mean distance of paternal mitochondria from the sperm DNA (Figure 8A) as well as significantly increased standard deviation of individual distances (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a finding from quantitative analysis of fixed embryos shown in Figure 8A.

claim: ATX-2 depletion resulted in significantly increased standard deviation of individual distances of paternal mitochondria from the sperm DNA.
source: ATX-2 depletion by each of the three methods resulted in a significantly increased mean distance of paternal mitochondria from the sperm DNA (Figure 8A) as well as significantly increased standard deviation of individual distances (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a finding from quantitative analysis of fixed embryos shown in Figure 8B.

claim: ATX-2 is required to maintain the integrity or cohesiveness of the ball of paternal mitochondria that surrounds the sperm DNA to resist external forces.
source: These results still support the hypothesis that ATX-2 is required to maintain the integrity or cohesiveness of the ball of paternal mitochondria that surrounds the sperm DNA to resist external forces.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ATX-2 depletion experiments.

claim: Among 24 time-lapse sequences of atx-2(AID +auxin) klp-7(RNAi) meiotic embryos, the ER envelope around the sperm DNA moved extensively in all cases.
source: Among 24 time-lapse sequences of atx-2(AID +auxin) klp-7(RNAi) meiotic embryos, the ER envelope around the sperm DNA moved extensively in all cases but came within a threshold distance of 5.5 µm (center to center) of the meiotic spindle in only five cases.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: In atx-2(AID +auxin) klp-7(RNAi) embryos, the ER envelope around the sperm DNA came within 5.5 µm of the meiotic spindle in only five cases out of 24.
source: Among 24 time-lapse sequences of atx-2(AID +auxin) klp-7(RNAi) meiotic embryos, the ER envelope around the sperm DNA moved extensively in all cases but came within a threshold distance of 5.5 µm (center to center) of the meiotic spindle in only five cases.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: In 5/5 cases where the sperm DNA came within 5.5 µm of the spindle in atx-2(AID +auxin) klp-7(RNAi) embryos, a bundle of microtubules extended from the meiotic spindle into the ER envelope around the sperm DNA, and the sperm DNA became stuck in this position.
source: In 5/5 of these cases, a bundle of microtubules extended from the meiotic spindle into the ER envelope around the sperm DNA, and the sperm DNA became stuck in this position (Figure 9A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 9A and B.

claim: In one case, the ER envelope around the sperm DNA was transiently captured by the meiosis I spindle and stretched in the direction of streaming.
source: In one case, the ER envelope around the sperm DNA was transiently captured by the meiosis I spindle and stretched in the direction of streaming (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 9C.

claim: After transient capture by the meiosis I spindle, the sperm DNA released, continued streaming, and was captured by the meiosis II spindle.
source: The sperm DNA then released, continued streaming, and was captured by the meiosis II spindle.
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging.

claim: All cases of stable capture in atx-2(AID +auxin) klp-7(RNAi) embryos caused a cell-cycle arrest.
source: All cases of stable capture caused a cell-cycle arrest so that the consequences of polar body extrusion could not be determined.
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: The maximum long-axis and short-axis displacement of the sperm contents at any cell-cycle time was increased in atx-2(AID) with auxin vs without auxin.
source: However, the maximum long-axis and short-axis displacement at any cell-cycle time was increased in atx-2(AID) with auxin vs without auxin (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: No spindle capture events were observed among 15 ATX-2 single depletion time-lapse sequences.
source: No spindle capture events were observed, however, among 15 ATX-2 single depletion time-lapse sequences and the closest distance between sperm and spindle was 8.2 µm with 1 hr auxin and 19.3 µm without auxin.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: The closest distance between sperm and spindle in ATX-2 single depletion was 8.2 µm with 1 hr auxin and 19.3 µm without auxin.
source: No spindle capture events were observed, however, among 15 ATX-2 single depletion time-lapse sequences and the closest distance between sperm and spindle was 8.2 µm with 1 hr auxin and 19.3 µm without auxin.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: The frequency of sperm capture by the meiotic spindle was significantly higher than wild-type controls in klp-7(RNAi) atx-2(AID) double-depleted embryos (p=0.011 Fisher's exact test).
source: The frequency of sperm capture by the meiotic spindle (Figure 9D) was significantly higher than wild-type controls in klp-7(RNAi) atx-2(AID) double-depleted embryos (p=0.011 Fisher's exact test).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from comparing capture frequencies shown in Figure 9D.

claim: Limiting cytoplasmic streaming and maintaining the integrity of the ball of paternal mitochondria are both important for preventing capture events between the meiotic spindle and sperm DNA.
source: Although the number of single mutant embryos analyzed was too low to demonstrate a significant difference between single and double mutant embryos, these results qualitatively support the hypothesis that limiting cytoplasmic streaming and maintaining the integrity of the ball of paternal mitochondria are both important for preventing capture events between the meiotic spindle and sperm DNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the double depletion experiments.

claim: The simplest hypothesis is that maternal and paternal cytoplasm might not mix during the 45 minutes from GVBD to pronucleus formation due to the high viscosity of cytoplasm.
source: The simplest hypothesis is that maternal and paternal cytoplasm might not mix during the 45 min from GVBD to pronucleus formation due to the high viscosity of cytoplasm.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed in the discussion.

claim: Attempts at measuring the cytoplasmic viscosity of the C. elegans zygote have revealed values from 0.67 to 1.0 Pa s.
source: Attempts at measuring the cytoplasmic viscosity of the C. elegans zygote have revealed values from 0.67 to 1.0 Pa s (Khatri et al., 2022; Daniels et al., 2006; Garzon-Coral et al., 2016) which are similar to the viscosity of 100% glycerol.
evidence: This is stated based on citations.

claim: The cytoplasmic viscosity of the C. elegans zygote is similar to the viscosity of 100% glycerol.
source: Attempts at measuring the cytoplasmic viscosity of the C. elegans zygote have revealed values from 0.67 to 1.0 Pa s (Khatri et al., 2022; Daniels et al., 2006; Garzon-Coral et al., 2016) which are similar to the viscosity of 100% glycerol.
evidence: This is a comparison made based on cited viscosity measurements.

claim: The sperm contents might be held together by a cytoskeleton-like matrix as proposed for the Balbiani body.
source: Alternatively, the sperm contents might be held together by a cytoskeleton-like matrix as proposed for the Balbiani body (Boke et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: An active process appears to allow the maternal ER to penetrate into the paternal cytoplasm to envelope the sperm DNA.
source: In either case, an active process appears to allow the maternal ER to penetrate into the paternal cytoplasm to envelope the sperm DNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that ER penetrates while other organelles are excluded.

claim: The capture of the sperm DNA by the meiotic spindle in ATX-2 KLP-7 double-depleted embryos suggests that the integrity of the exclusion zone around the sperm DNA might insulate the sperm DNA from spindle microtubules.
source: The capture of the sperm DNA by the meiotic spindle in ATX-2 KLP-7 double-depleted embryos (Figure 9) suggests that the integrity of the exclusion zone around the sperm DNA might insulate the sperm DNA from spindle microtubules.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion drawn from the double depletion experiments.

claim: The effect of ATX-2 depletion must be on the egg and not on the sperm because the paternal mitochondria observed to scatter are from wild-type males.
source: Because the paternal mitochondria observed to scatter are from wild-type males, the effect of ATX-2 depletion must be on the egg and not on the sperm.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the experimental design.

claim: A maternal ER envelope around the sperm DNA was observed in all ATX-2-depleted embryos.
source: Although ATX-2 depletion alters ER morphology (Del Castillo et al., 2019) we still observed a maternal ER envelope around the sperm DNA in all ATX-2-depleted embryos.
evidence: This is a finding from imaging ATX-2-depleted embryos.

claim: ATX-2 plays roles in translational regulation.
source: ATX-2 also plays roles in translational regulation (Ciosk et al., 2004), germline proliferation (Maine et al., 2004), cytokinesis (Gnazzo et al., 2016), centrosome size (Stubenvoll et al., 2016), and fat metabolism (Bar et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: ATX-2 plays roles in germline proliferation.
source: ATX-2 also plays roles in translational regulation (Ciosk et al., 2004), germline proliferation (Maine et al., 2004), cytokinesis (Gnazzo et al., 2016), centrosome size (Stubenvoll et al., 2016), and fat metabolism (Bar et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: ATX-2 plays roles in cytokinesis.
source: ATX-2 also plays roles in translational regulation (Ciosk et al., 2004), germline proliferation (Maine et al., 2004), cytokinesis (Gnazzo et al., 2016), centrosome size (Stubenvoll et al., 2016), and fat metabolism (Bar et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: ATX-2 plays roles in centrosome size regulation.
source: ATX-2 also plays roles in translational regulation (Ciosk et al., 2004), germline proliferation (Maine et al., 2004), cytokinesis (Gnazzo et al., 2016), centrosome size (Stubenvoll et al., 2016), and fat metabolism (Bar et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: ATX-2 plays roles in fat metabolism.
source: ATX-2 also plays roles in translational regulation (Ciosk et al., 2004), germline proliferation (Maine et al., 2004), cytokinesis (Gnazzo et al., 2016), centrosome size (Stubenvoll et al., 2016), and fat metabolism (Bar et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: The effects of ATX-2 could be extremely indirect.
source: Thus the effects of ATX-2 could be extremely indirect.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the multiple roles of ATX-2.

claim: C. elegans ovulate every 23 minutes.
source: Because C. elegans ovulate every 23 min (McCarter et al., 1999), however, our rapid 1 hr depletion would only affect the three most mature oocytes.
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: The rapid 1 hr ATX-2 depletion would only affect the three most mature oocytes.
source: Because C. elegans ovulate every 23 min (McCarter et al., 1999), however, our rapid 1 hr depletion would only affect the three most mature oocytes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ovulation rate.

claim: ATX-2 might regulate 'the integrity of the cytoplasm' analogous to the action of ANC-1 in the C. elegans hypodermis.
source: A speculative possibility is that ATX-2 regulates 'the integrity of the cytoplasm' analogous to the action of ANC-1 in the C. elegans hypodermis (Hao et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: ATX-2 might act as part of the RNA-dependent ER-associated TIS granule network because it is an RNA-binding protein with intrinsically disordered domains.
source: Because ATX-2 is an RNA-binding protein with intrinsically disordered domains, it might act as part of the RNA-dependent ER-associated TIS granule network (Ma et al., 2021; Ma and Mayr, 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis proposed in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: In control embryos, the sperm contents rarely came near the meiotic spindle in agreement with a previous study that found that male and female pronuclei rarely form next to each other.
source: In control embryos, the sperm contents rarely came near the meiotic spindle (18 µm closest distance, see text above) in agreement with a previous study that found that male and female pronuclei rarely form next to each other (Kimura and Kimura, 2020).
evidence: This is a finding from control experiments that agrees with a previous study.

claim: Streaming of the sperm contents was most commonly restricted to a jostling motion with little net displacement, circular streaming in the short-axis of the embryo, or long-axis streaming in which the sperm turned away from the spindle before the halfway point of the embryo.
source: Streaming of the sperm contents was most commonly restricted to a jostling motion with little net displacement, circular streaming in the short-axis of the embryo, or long-axis streaming in which the sperm turned away from the spindle before the halfway point of the embryo (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 5.

claim: Depletion of MEI-1 or KLP-7 resulted in longer excursions of the sperm contents in the long-axis of the embryo toward the spindle.
source: Depletion of MEI-1 or KLP-7 resulted in longer excursions of the sperm contents in the long-axis of the embryo toward the spindle (Figure 5) but frequent capture of the sperm by the spindle was only observed in mei-1(RNAi) (Figures 5 and 9D).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 5.

claim: Frequent capture of the sperm by the spindle was only observed in mei-1(RNAi).
source: Depletion of MEI-1 or KLP-7 resulted in longer excursions of the sperm contents in the long-axis of the embryo toward the spindle (Figure 5) but frequent capture of the sperm by the spindle was only observed in mei-1(RNAi) (Figures 5 and 9D).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figures 5 and 9D.

claim: mei-1(RNAi) affects the positioning of the spindle within the embryo.
source: This may be because mei-1(RNAi) affects the positioning of the spindle within the embryo (Yang et al., 2003) or because the altered structure of the mei-1(RNAi) spindle allows spindle microtubules to capture chromosomes further from the spindle center.
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: The altered structure of the mei-1(RNAi) spindle may allow spindle microtubules to capture chromosomes further from the spindle center.
source: This may be because mei-1(RNAi) affects the positioning of the spindle within the embryo (Yang et al., 2003) or because the altered structure of the mei-1(RNAi) spindle allows spindle microtubules to capture chromosomes further from the spindle center.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed capture events.

claim: In capture events observed after double depletion of ATX-2 and KLP-7, a bundle of microtubules was discernible extending from the spindle into the ER envelope surrounding the sperm DNA.
source: In capture events observed after double depletion of ATX-2 and KLP-7, a bundle of microtubules was discernible extending from the spindle into the ER envelope surrounding the sperm DNA (Figure 9).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 9.

claim: Such microtubule bundles were not observed in mei-1(RNAi) capture events, likely because of the previously reported low density of microtubules in mei-1(RNAi) spindles.
source: Such bundles were not observed in mei-1(RNAi) capture events (Figure 5), likely because of the previously reported low density of microtubules in mei-1(RNAi) spindles (McNally et al., 2006; Srayko et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a finding from time-lapse imaging and an explanation based on citations.

claim: The only reported example of premature interaction between the sperm contents and the oocyte meiotic spindle outside of C. elegans is the extrusion of sperm DNA into the second polar body when sperm was injected adjacent to the mouse metaphase II spindle.
source: To our knowledge, the only reported example of premature interaction between the sperm contents and the oocyte meiotic spindle outside of C. elegans is the extrusion of sperm DNA into the second polar body when sperm was injected adjacent to the mouse metaphase II spindle (Mori et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: Close proximity of the sperm contents to the meiotic spindle and apparent capture events in C. elegans has been reported in only 20–25% of mei-1(RNAi), klp-7 atx-2 double depletion or kca-1(RNAi) meiotic embryos.
source: Close proximity of the sperm contents to the meiotic spindle and apparent capture events in C. elegans has been reported in only 20–25% of mei-1(RNAi), klp-7 atx-2 double depletion (Figure 9D) or kca-1(RNAi) (McNally et al., 2012) meiotic embryos.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from this study and a previous study.

claim: In the case of kca-1(RNAi), premature sperm asters were implicated in the capture events.
source: In the case of kca-1(RNAi), premature sperm asters were implicated in the capture events (McNally et al., 2012), however, kca-1(RNAi) blocks cytoplasmic streaming (McNally et al., 2010) and thus likely reduces the probability of the sperm contents moving close to the spindle, which is also mispositioned in kca-1(RNAi) (Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated based on citations.

claim: kca-1(RNAi) blocks cytoplasmic streaming.
source: In the case of kca-1(RNAi), premature sperm asters were implicated in the capture events (McNally et al., 2012), however, kca-1(RNAi) blocks cytoplasmic streaming (McNally et al., 2010) and thus likely reduces the probability of the sperm contents moving close to the spindle, which is also mispositioned in kca-1(RNAi) (Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: The spindle is mispositioned in kca-1(RNAi).
source: In the case of kca-1(RNAi), premature sperm asters were implicated in the capture events (McNally et al., 2012), however, kca-1(RNAi) blocks cytoplasmic streaming (McNally et al., 2010) and thus likely reduces the probability of the sperm contents moving close to the spindle, which is also mispositioned in kca-1(RNAi) (Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: Close proximity of the sperm DNA with the meiotic spindle was reported in a small fraction of fixed pfn-1(RNAi) embryos where increased mobility of the sperm contents was also reported but actual capture events were not reported.
source: Close proximity of the sperm DNA with the meiotic spindle was also reported in a small fraction of fixed pfn-1(RNAi) embryos where increased mobility of the sperm contents was also reported but actual capture events were not reported (Panzica et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.

claim: An 80-µm diameter mouse zygote has a volume 16 times greater than a 50-µm × 25-µm ellipsoid C. elegans zygote.
source: An 80- µm diameter mouse zygote has a volume 16 times greater than a 50-µm × 25- µm ellipsoid C. elegans zygote and a 120 µm diameter human zygote has a volume 55 times greater than a C. elegans zygote [using the equation 4/3 Π(ra)(rb)(rc)].
evidence: This is a calculation based on the volume equation for ellipsoids.

claim: A 120 µm diameter human zygote has a volume 55 times greater than a C. elegans zygote.
source: An 80- µm diameter mouse zygote has a volume 16 times greater than a 50-µm × 25- µm ellipsoid C. elegans zygote and a 120 µm diameter human zygote has a volume 55 times greater than a C. elegans zygote [using the equation 4/3 Π(ra)(rb)(rc)].
evidence: This is a calculation based on the volume equation for ellipsoids.

claim: None of the time-lapse sequences of sperm capture by the meiotic spindle resulted in the extrusion of paternal DNA into a polar body, likely because of the pleiotropic effects of depleting MEI-1, KLP-7, or ATX-2.
source: None of our time-lapse sequences of sperm capture by the meiotic spindle resulted in the extrusion of paternal DNA into a polar body as was observed when sperm was injected next to the meiotic spindle of mouse oocytes (Mori et al., 2021), likely because of the pleiotropic effects of depleting MEI-1, KLP-7, or ATX-2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results and comparison with mouse studies.

claim: Many of the reported kca-1(RNAi) capture events also resulted in an arrest.
source: Many of the reported kca-1(RNAi) capture events also resulted in an arrest (McNally et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated based on a citation.
